content:
maya: Quick design review — proposing a compact p95 strip above the heatmap instead of side-by-side. Thoughts?
sam: I like compact for narrow screens. Does it still read as 'trend first, density second'?
maya: That’s the goal. idea: p95 sparkline + current value pill on top, heatmap fills the rest. keeps vertical rhythm.
liam: Accessibility question — will the heatmap maintain color contrast for colorblind users?
maya: Good call. Plan is to use a diverging palette with >=4.5:1 and also offer a pattern overlay option.
devon: Pattern overlay could get noisy. Could we instead add an accessible alternative view (high-contrast monochrome bins) behind an a11y toggle?
aisha: +1 for a toggle. Also, keyboard focus order: make the time-range picker first, then p95, then heatmap.
sam: Time-range picker being first feels right. We're seeing people change ranges often. Maybe add 1-click presets (Last 1h, 6h, 24h) as chips.
maya: Presets are in the mock. Also thinking of a sticky 'live tail' toggle that pins to tailing mode (auto-scroll).
liam: For sampling controls, the current wording 'Sampling rate' confused a PM — suggest 'Trace sampling' vs 'Event sampling'?
aisha: Or 'Request sampling' — short and less ambiguous in the context of latency metrics.
devon: UX nit: the p95 tooltip says "Median of tail" in current copy — that's misleading. Suggest: "95th percentile latency: 95% of requests were faster than this value"
sam: Much clearer. Also, heatmap hover should show bin range + count + example endpoint.
maya: Agree. Example hover content mock: 
```
Range: 120–160ms
Count: 1,234 (3.2%)
Top endpoint: /api/generate
```
liam: Can we include a tiny sparklines stack in each heatmap column on hover? low-fi but helpful.
aisha: Performance concern — generating those on every hover might be heavy. Maybe precompute per-column summary server-side.
devon: Yep, precompute + cache. Redwood Console already has the summaries endpoint.
maya: Design-bot: uploaded new canvas with compact p95 strip and presets (link: https://figma.redwood/designs/latency-compact-strip).
design-bot: file uploaded by maya — https://figma.redwood/designs/latency-compact-strip (preview available).
sam: A11y checklist: roles for live regions when live tail updates numbers, aria-label on presets, focus-visible styles for keyboard, colorblind palette test.
liam: One more: default sampling should be 5% not 1% for dashboard-level so heatmap isn't empty for low-volume routes. We can expose a per-route override.
aisha: 5% seems reasonable. Add a short microcopy under sampling control: "Higher sampling = more accurate heatmap; increases cost."
maya: Great. I'll update the mock and add copy suggestions. Final ask: designers — can we test compact strip at 1280x720 and 1024x768? devs — can you confirm precompute endpoint exists for per-column summaries?
sam: I can check infra tomorrow.
devon: I'll confirm backend caching and add an opt-in param.
liam: I'll run colorblind sim on the palette and share results.
aisha: I'll draft the microcopy and aria labels.
maya: Thanks all — will iterate and post an updated mock here. :sparkles:
